title: The Best Seller Report
prompt: sales = [("mon", "pen", 4), ("mon", "book", 2), ("tue", "pen", 3), ("wed", "bag", 5), ("wed", "book", 7)] — tuples of (day, item, qty). Write report(sales) returning a dict with keys: "total" (all units sold), "best_item" (item with the highest total units; ties -> the one that REACHED its total first), and "busiest_day" (day with the most units; ties -> alphabetically first).

tests.name: report is correct
tests.code:
r = report(sales)
assert r["total"] == 21, f"total: {r}"
assert r["best_item"] == "book", f"best_item: {r}"
assert r["busiest_day"] == "wed", f"busiest_day: {r}"
r2 = report([("mon", "a", 1), ("tue", "b", 1)])
assert r2["best_item"] == "a", f"tie -> a's last sale (mon) precedes b's (tue): {r2}"
assert r2["busiest_day"] == "mon", f"day tie -> alphabetical: {r2}"
r5 = report([("tue", "a", 1), ("mon", "b", 1)])
assert r5["busiest_day"] == "mon", f"day tie -> alphabetical, not arrival: {r5}"
r6 = report([("mon", "a", 1), ("tue", "b", 2), ("wed", "a", 1)])
assert r6["best_item"] == "b", f"totals tie at 2; b's last sale (tue) precedes a's (wed): {r6}"
tests.hint: track units AND the index of each item's LAST sale; on equal totals prefer the item whose last sale came EARLIER (min by (-units, last_idx)). Days: sort by (-units, name).
